author: copilot
body:
The API already exposed ref-to-commit resolution, but it did not provide a way to enumerate the refs a client can choose from. This change adds a companion endpoint to list repository branches and tags in a normalized API shape.

- **API surface**
  - Adds `POST /api/jobs/refs`
  - Accepts `{ "repo": "owner/repo" }`
  - Returns branch and tag refs with:
    - canonical ref name
    - ref type
    - resolved commit SHA
    - short SHA

- **Git ref discovery**
  - Introduces `listRepositoryRefs()` in `repoProcessor`
  - Uses `git ls-remote --heads --tags` to enumerate remote refs
  - Normalizes annotated tags so the response contains a single `refs/tags/<tag>` entry with the dereferenced commit

- **Type contracts**
  - Adds request/response types for the new endpoint
  - Defines a structured `GitRefSummary` payload shared across route and service code

- **Docs**
  - Extends the README API section with the new refs-listing endpoint and response shape

```json
POST /api/jobs/refs
{
  "repo": "facebook/react"
}
```

```json
{
  "repo": "facebook/react",
  "refs": [
    {
      "name": "main",
      "ref": "refs/heads/main",
      "type": "branch",
      "commit": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
      "commitShort": "0123456"
    },
    {
      "name": "v1.0.0",
      "ref": "refs/tags/v1.0.0",
      "type": "tag",
      "commit": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
      "commitShort": "0123456"
    }
  ]
}
```

author: th4s
body:
This PR fixes the OT allocation in `crates/zk` for `prover` and `verifier`.

Currently the OT allocation for the quicksilver check assumes that all circuits are executable, but in practice we allocate circuits, whose inputs are committed at a later stage of the program flow and thus are not executable when `execute` is called.

The consequence is that a check for the AND gates is done every time `execute` is called, although all of them would have nicely fit into a single `batchsize`. This leads to an excess consumption of OTs, more than calculated on the basis that all circuits are executable. We get an OT allocation error.

The fix is to reallocate those OTs if this case happens.

author: slin1237
body:
## Summary

Implements API-key-aware `/v1/models` for BYOK (bring your own key) flows. When a bearer token is present, the gateway fans out to all healthy external upstreams to discover available models. Falls back to self-hosted registry models if upstreams fail or return nothing.

Closes #691

## What changed

- **`model_gateway/src/routers/router_manager.rs`**: Rewrote `get_models` to extract bearer token and fan out to upstreams. Added `fetch_upstream_models` (deduplicates by URL, parallel fan-out) and `fetch_models_from` (per-upstream GET with `apply_provider_headers`). Added `client: reqwest::Client` field.
- **`crates/protocols/src/models.rs`**: Added `ListModelsResponse::parse_upstream` — handles both OpenAI and Anthropic response schemas (`data[].id`) and converts to `Vec<ModelCard>` with provider inference.
- **Removed `get_models` from all individual routers** (http, pd, openai, anthropic, gemini) — `RouterManager` is now the single implementation.
- **Deleted `model_gateway/src/routers/anthropic/models.rs`** — only contained `handle_list_models`, no longer needed.
- **Updated test** `policy_registry_integration.rs` for new `RouterManager::new` signature.

## Why

Users sending their own provider API keys should discover which models are available upstream, not just locally-registered ones. The previous implementation had each router duplicating `/v1/models` logic with no upstream discovery.

## How

`/v1/models` is a public route (no auth middleware). When a bearer token is present:
1. `RouterManager::fetch_upstream_models` gets healthy external workers, deduplicates by URL
2. Fans out `GET /v1/models` to each unique upstream in parallel
3. `apply_provider_headers` handles provider-specific auth (Anthropic `x-api-key` vs standard `Bearer`)
4. `ListModelsResponse::parse_upstream` (protocols crate) parses both OpenAI and Anthropic JSON schemas
5. If any upstream returns models, those are returned; otherwise falls back to registry

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo build -p smg` — compiles cleanly
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p smg --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — no warnings
- [ ] `cargo test -p smg` — existing tests pass
- [ ] Manual: `curl /v1/models` (no auth) → registry models
- [ ] Manual: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <provider-key>" /v1/models` → upstream models (if external workers configured)
- [ ] Manual: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <invalid-key>" /v1/models` → falls back to registry models

* **Bug Fixes & Improvements**

author: vltbaudbot
body:
## Problem

After switching CI runners from `ubuntu-latest` (x64) to `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (arm64) in [646f3c6](https://github.com/vltpkg/benchmarks/commit/646f3c649076f191a09ca07771eb2568ea9decf8), the hyperfine install was changed from a manual v1.19.0 amd64 `.deb` to `apt-get install -y hyperfine` in [bbc7b5c](https://github.com/vltpkg/benchmarks/commit/bbc7b5cf17f5a2549c43a65bf0270cf874071c3e).

Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) ships **hyperfine 1.18.0** via apt, but the benchmark scripts use the `--conclude` flag which was [introduced in hyperfine 1.19.0](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/releases/tag/v1.19.0). This causes every benchmark job to fail with:

```
error: unexpected argument '--conclude' found

  tip: to pass '--conclude' as a value, use '-- --conclude'

Usage: hyperfine --ignore-failure --time-unit <UNIT> --export-json <FILE> --warmup <NUM> --runs <NUM> --setup <CMD> <command>...
```

Ref: https://github.com/vltpkg/benchmarks/actions/runs/22918303468

## Fix

Install hyperfine 1.19.0 directly from GitHub releases with architecture detection (`dpkg --print-architecture`) so it works on both amd64 and arm64 runners:

```bash
HYPERFINE_VERSION_TAG="v1.19.0"
ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture)  # amd64 or arm64
wget -q "https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/releases/download/${HYPERFINE_VERSION_TAG}/hyperfine_${HYPERFINE_VERSION_TAG#v}_${ARCH}.deb" -O /tmp/hyperfine.deb
sudo dpkg -i /tmp/hyperfine.deb
```

## `--conclude` usage

The flag is used across all 11 variation scripts:
- `clean.sh`, `cache.sh`, `lockfile.sh`, `node_modules.sh`
- `cache+lockfile.sh`, `cache+node_modules.sh`, `lockfile+node_modules.sh`, `cache+lockfile+node_modules.sh`
- `registry-clean.sh`, `registry-lockfile.sh`

# Issue body

This issue is **PR 5 of 6** in the staged rewrite of the AI competition system.

Full sequence for context:

1. PR1 — competition AI foundation (types + architecture)
2. PR2 — houseguest competition profiles
3. PR3 — minigame AI metadata / qualification layer
4. PR4 — profile-based AI simulation engine
5. **PR5 — light dynamic season modifiers (this PR)**
6. PR6 — competition scheduling diversity + telemetry/balancing tools

What already exists from prior PRs:

* a typed competition AI foundation
* competition profiles for houseguests
* minigame AI metadata / registry
* a deterministic profile-based AI simulation engine using profile + minigame metadata + seed

This PR should add **small, temporary, season-level performance modifiers** so AI houseguests feel more like real contestants and less like static stat blocks.

## High-level goal

Add a light season dynamics layer that influences AI competition outcomes through temporary modifiers such as:

* season form / momentum
* confidence
* fatigue

Potentially also lightweight pressure handling, but only as a bounded temporary modifier built on top of the current simulation engine.

Important scope boundary:
These modifiers should be **small and temporary**. They should not permanently rewrite a houseguest’s core competition identity.

Base competition profiles remain the long-term identity layer.
This PR only adds temporary season-state effects.

---

## Problem

Even with profile-based simulation, AI can still feel too static if players always perform according to their baseline profile only.

Real contestants fluctuate:

* a player can be on a hot streak
* a player can lose confidence after repeated failures
* a player can be slightly worn down after repeated competition participation
* some moments feel higher pressure than others

Without a lightweight season-state layer, seasons may become more predictable and less narratively believable.

---

## Goal of this PR

Add a bounded, deterministic season modifier layer that adjusts AI competition performance based on temporary state, without changing the underlying permanent competition profiles.

These dynamic modifiers should:

* make contestants feel alive
* introduce believable streaks/slumps
* remain subtle enough to avoid chaos
* remain deterministic / seed-compatible
* remain inspectable and easy to tune later

---

## Non-goals for this PR

Do not implement the following here:

* do not permanently mutate base competition profiles
* do not add a full rating / Elo-like progression system
* do not add competition scheduling logic
* do not add telemetry dashboards or balancing harnesses
* do not rewrite the season structure
* do not add large UI systems around these modifiers
* do not create dramatic rubber-banding against the user
* do not make AI react after seeing the user’s exact score
* do not turn this into a complex psychological simulation

This PR should stay intentionally lightweight.

---

## Core design rules

### 1) Base profiles remain static

The competition profiles introduced earlier represent each houseguest’s core identity and must remain unchanged.

Example:
A mental player should not permanently become a physical beast because of a few wins.

### 2) Dynamic modifiers are temporary

Dynamic modifiers should apply only within the current season / current run.

### 3) Modifiers must be small

These should gently tilt outcomes, not dominate them.

As a rule of thumb:

* dynamic effects should usually influence outcomes by a modest amount
* the base profile + minigame weights should still be the primary driver

### 4) Deterministic

All modifier effects that influence simulation must remain deterministic given the same state + seed.

### 5) Centralized

The logic for dynamic season modifiers should be implemented in the AI competition module / store layer cleanly, not scattered.

author: acidleroy
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**


Kubernetes allows some skew between the control plane and kubelets, but [kubeadm's own skew policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/production-environment/tools/kubeadm/create-cluster-kubeadm/#version-skew-policy) requires the **kubeadm binary used for `kubeadm join` to match** the kubeadm used when the cluster was created or last upgraded on that path—so you cannot rely on an older kubeadm on the worker when the control plane is newer.

That conflicts with real Cluster API flows (e.g. scaling or remediating workers still on an older Kubernetes while the control plane has moved ahead), as discussed in [#13315](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/issues/13315).

This PR:

- **Adds a new `contentFormat` field to `spec.files`** with two values: `Raw` (default, content used verbatim as today) and `Template` (content rendered as Go `text/template`). Template data includes **`{{ .controlPlane.version }}`** (the control plane Kubernetes version, normalized to a `v`-prefixed semver, e.g. `v1.35.0`), so operators can wire their own steps (scripts, package installs, downloads) to install a **kubeadm binary that matches the control plane** before `kubeadm join` runs—without CAPI prescribing a single install mechanism.
- **Resolves the control plane Kubernetes version** from the cluster's `controlPlaneRef` (e.g. `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.version`), read via an **APIReader** (no extra informer/cache for `KubeadmControlPlane`). This is the single source for the `{{ .controlPlane.version }}` template variable. When there is no `controlPlaneRef` or the referenced object does not expose `spec.version`, the `controlPlane` key is simply **omitted** from the template data (no fallback), so templates can guard with `{{ if .controlPlane }}`. Unexpected read errors fail reconciliation and surface on the existing `KubeadmConfigDataSecretAvailable` condition (no new condition is introduced).
- **JoinConfiguration is still marshalled with the joining Machine's own Kubernetes version** (unchanged behavior). A newer kubeadm binary reads an older JoinConfiguration API version fine, so the control plane version does not need to drive the join config schema—it only feeds `spec.files` templates.
- **RBAC** for the kubeadm bootstrap controller to read `KubeadmControlPlane` (no `/status`) where needed for version resolution.
- **E2E template** for `cluster-template-topology-kubeadm-version` moved into its own kustomize sub-folder (consistent with other topology templates) and wired into the `generate-e2e-templates-main` Makefile target.
- **Tests**: unit coverage for template **parse** vs **execute** failures in `spec.files` and for the `controlPlane.version` resolution paths, and **E2E** coverage (`KubeadmJoinOldNodes` + `clusterclass-quick-start-kubeadm-version`) that upgrades the control plane and then joins an older worker which fetches the matching kubeadm via the rendered file—demonstrating the pattern end-to-end.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CP as Control plane (newer K8s)
    participant BC as Kubeadm bootstrap controller
    participant W as Worker (older image / kubelet)

    BC->>CP: Read KubeadmControlPlane.spec.version (APIReader)
    CP-->>BC: e.g. v1.35.0
    BC->>BC: Build join data (Machine version) + render spec.files templates
    BC->>W: Render spec.files (contentFormat: Template) e.g. fetch script with {{ .controlPlane.version }}
    Note over W: preKubeadmCommands (operator-defined)
    W->>W: Install/fetch kubeadm matching CP version
    W->>CP: kubeadm join (binary matches policy)
```

Produces a cinematic 30-second raytraced video of the M35 truck falling 500 m onto `terra` terrain, landing, and settling — with ground horizon visible, perspective projection, and realistic shaders. All inputs and a resumable render script are checked in alongside the final video.

## New files (`brlcad/misc/simulate/`)

- **`cinematic_setup.tcl`** — builds the simulation `.g` database with material overrides (`inherit=1`):
  - Terrain: earthy brown RGB(95,75,50), `plastic {sh 2 sp .05 di .95}` (matte dirt)
  - Truck: US Army olive drab RGB(56,72,30) ≈ FS 34087, `plastic {sh 12 sp .25 di .75}` (painted metal)

- **`cinematic_render.py`** — "Trackside Vantage" fixed-world camera at terrain level, 150 m from the landing zone:
  - Perspective `35°` half-angle (70° FOV ≈ 28 mm cinema lens) via `rt -c "perspective 35"`
  - Sky-blue background `rt -C 100/150/220`; dynamic viewsize = 2× eye-to-truck distance each frame
  - Camera elevation naturally sweeps +73° (truck 500 m aloft) → −1.7° (truck at rest), giving the ground-horizon orientation cue throughout the landing sequence

- **`cinematic_sim.sh`** — master script: 300 steps × 0.1 s = 30 s physics, renders 1280×720 at 10 fps, assembles H.264 CRF 18 video

- **`resume_cinematic.sh`** — fully resumable variant; skips already-present database, `.g` frame snapshots, rendered PNGs, and final video so interrupted runs can be continued without re-doing completed work

- **`truck_terrain_cinematic.mp4`** — final 30-second 1280×720 video (772 KB)

## Updated files

- **`run_sim.sh`** — adds `BRLCAD_ROOT` and `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` so the `ged-simulate` Bullet plugin resolves at runtime on Ubuntu with system `libbullet-dev` (requires `BRLCAD_BUNDLED_LIBS=SYSTEM` at configure time to match the single-precision float ABI)

## Build requirements

```bash
# System deps
sudo apt-get install -y libbullet-dev ffmpeg

# CMake flags
-DBRLCAD_ENABLE_BULLET=ON -DBRLCAD_BUNDLED_LIBS=SYSTEM \
-DBULLET_DYNAMICS_LIBRARY=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libBulletDynamics.so \
-DBULLET_COLLISION_LIBRARY=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libBulletCollision.so \
-DBULLET_MATH_LIBRARY=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libLinearMath.so \
-DBULLET_SOFTBODY_LIBRARY=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libBulletSoftBody.so
```

To reproduce or extend the render:
```bash
cd brlcad/misc/simulate
./resume_cinematic.sh /path/to/brlcad-build [output_dir]
```

author: chromium-wpt-export-bot
body:
This patch ensures that focus navigation correctly enters and exits an
open popover even if its invoker element becomes non-focusable (e.g.,
by setting the 'inert' attribute or 'disabled' state).

Previously, focus navigation relied on the invoker being focusable to
treat it as a focus scope owner for the popover. By removing the
focusability requirement in Element::GetOpenPopoverTarget and updating
FocusController to recognize non-keyboard-focusable invokers as scope
owners, focus now correctly moves into the popover when tabbing from
elements before it in the DOM.

Changes:
- Element::GetOpenPopoverTarget() no longer checks IsFocusable().
- FocusController now treats non-keyboard-focusable popover invokers
  as focus scope owners.
- Updated FindFocusableElementAcrossFocusScopes logic to handle
  entering popover scopes via non-focusable owners.
- Added a new Web Platform Test to verify focus navigation with an
  inert popover invoker.
